chapter_title: Chương 284: 0285【Panda Burning Incense, bạn đã nghe nói chưa?】

segments.title: Chương 284: 0285【Panda Burning Incense, bạn đã nghe nói chưa?】
segments.content:
Saturday.

Chen Guiliang had proper business to attend to in the morning, so Tao Xue didn't come to the company. Instead, she went to hang out with an old classmate of hers from Renmin University. That was the unfortunate kid who had scored top marks in the city's college entrance exams but hadn't dared to apply to Tsinghua or Peking University.

Chen Guiliang was busy signing various documents. Lu Zhihui was about to head to the Cayman Islands with their lawyers to register the company.

By mid-morning, things were more or less settled.

Chen Guiliang casually opened a website to check the financial news, only to see the "2006 Forbes China Rich List," which had just been released, as the top headline on the finance channel.

Chen Guiliang quickly scanned the list, then moved his mouse to the top right corner and closed the page.

Forbes clearly didn't understand China. It was even more unreliable than the already very unreliable Hurun Report.

This year's richest man in China according to Forbes was Old Huang, the one who was about to go to jail.

The entire list included nearly 400 people, but only 15 of them were from the IT industry. They even included Yang Lan and her husband, with Forbes saying they were involved in the internet and media.

Among the top ten richest people on the list, half were in real estate.

Ding Sanshi, the highest-ranked person from the IT industry, was only ranked 12th on the China Rich List.

As for Chen Guiliang, of course he wasn't on the list!

However, on the "Hurun Rich List" from half a month ago, Chen Guiliang was ranked 438th.

This year, nearly 70 people were tied for 438th place by Hurun, all with assets of 800 million RMB... Although Forbes also had a bunch of people with 800 million, they really didn't have as many as Hurun.

When the Hurun list was first released, some netizens noticed this ridiculous situation because of Chen Guiliang and even posted a picture of the list on Hainei to poke fun at it.

Chen Guiliang's nickname was changed by those mischievous netizens from "Chen Shiyi" (Chen Ten Billion) to "Chen Bayi" (Chen Eight Hundred Million).

The Hurun list was actually quite reasonable. For unlisted companies, they generally calculated based on the last round of financing and would even discount it, only counting 60% of the valuation. Adding in Game Science's assets, Hurun estimated Chen Guiliang's total wealth at 800 million.

By the way, Zhou Hongwei was also at 800 million on the Hurun list, and similarly wasn't selected for this year's Forbes list.

Not long after Chen Guiliang closed the webpage, Zhou Hongwei called to complain, "Damn it, Forbes is so arrogant. Little brother, have you seen this year's Forbes list?"

"I've seen it," Chen Guiliang said.

Zhou Hongwei said, "Neither of us made it."

Chen Guiliang chuckled, "That's not bad. Wu Ying from UTStarcom didn't make it either."

Wu Ying, who had once overshadowed both Pony Ma and Jack Ma, had a company with a market cap of $26 billion at its peak.

Because mobile phones had become dirt cheap, sales of his PHS phones plummeted. He was having a rough time now. He was also at 800 million on the Hurun list, tied with Chen Guiliang.

Zhou Hongwei sighed, "It's a real pity about Wu Ying. Back then, he was the leading figure in China's high-tech enterprises."

Chen Guiliang said, "He bet on the wrong horse. He can't blame anyone."

Wu Ying believed that China was still relatively underdeveloped and that more than half of the Chinese people couldn't afford mobile phones. He thought that even if phone prices dropped, it wouldn't happen that quickly.

So his conclusion was: PHS phones would still sell for many more years.

Thus, while continuing to develop PHS technology, he also invested in or acquired companies with mobile phone-related technologies. He planned to take another six or seven years to complete the transition from PHS to mobile phones.

Who knew that China's development would be so rapid and transformative!

Of course, Wu Ying was still a wealthy man. The companies he had personally invested in included Cmsmc, Ht-Gd, Huayi Brothers, 58.com, and so on.

Zhou Hongwei extended an invitation, "Want to go shooting next weekend? It's been a while since we played live-action CS."

"I'm not free recently," Chen Guiliang politely declined.

"Boring." After saying a few more words, Zhou Hongwei hung up, probably to ask someone else to go shooting.

Chen Guiliang sat in front of his computer, muttering to himself, "Zhou Hongwei... 360... Antivirus... Panda Burning Incense..."

That national treasure that loved to burn incense should be coming soon.

Who among those who lived through that era hadn't heard of Panda Burning Incense?

This thing even made it onto the "Xinwen Lianbo" nightly news.

Chen Guiliang himself had a painful experience with it. His graduation thesis had been wiped out by Panda Burning Incense! He had to rewrite it in the end.

Having been reborn, and now running a company, he had to be on guard.

As early as six months ago, Chen Guiliang had talked to Guo Feng and Dong Qianqiu, and even had them consult more professional experts. He then issued a series of orders that left the employees somewhat bewildered.

For example, updating Microsoft's system patches immediately. Requiring all internal company file transfers to use the Jingkai collaborative platform, and strictly forbidding the random use of USB flash drives...

The Jingkai collaborative platform was an enterprise information software developed by Wang Zhidong after he left Sina. At a Peking University alumni entrepreneurship forum, Wang Zhidong had taken the opportunity to pitch his product. Chen Guiliang agreed to a three-month free trial and had been a paying customer ever since.

Panda Burning Incense would also tamper with webpage file code and game clients. For this reason, Chen Guiliang had specifically hired several programmers to develop a real-time webpage monitoring system and a self-verification module for the game clients.

Chen Guiliang called Ao Yanchen into his office. "Starting today, no one is allowed to bring a USB flash drive to the company. I'll be the one to decide when this ban is lifted."

"Are you trying to prevent people from stealing files?" Ao Yanchen asked, confused.

Chen Guiliang said, "You could say that. During the preparations for the IPO, it's better to be cautious with everything."

This reason couldn't be used at Game Science.

It didn't matter if he played the role of a clairvoyant immortal for once. When the time came, he would just say that he got a heads-up from a friend at an antivirus software company.

A sample of the Panda Burning Incense virus had already been discovered last month. In a few more days, Rising Antivirus would also get a sample.

However, most computer users weren't taking it seriously, and the virus was constantly evolving into new variants.

As noon approached, Chen Guiliang drove towards Renmin University.

"Senior, we're over here!" Tao Xue stood by the roadside, waving.

Chen Guiliang drove the car over and stopped.

Tao Xue made the introductions, "This is my high school classmate, Li Qian. She was the top liberal arts student in our city this year. She was just a bit conservative with her university application, otherwise she would have gone to Tsinghua or Peking University. Li Qian, this is Senior Chen."

Li Qian smiled and said, "Does Senior Chen even need an introduction? I don't know how many times the principal has mentioned him."

Tao Xue said, "It's not just the principal. The owner of the book rental store outside the school is always saying he knows Chen Guiliang. He even claims that the reason Chen Guiliang was able to win first prize in the essay competition was because he often bought and read books from his store."

"Haha, I've heard the owner say that too. I usually buy 'Du Zhe' magazine from him," Li Qian laughed.

Chen Guiliang also smiled. "Get in the car, I'll take you guys to eat."

The two girls got in, and Tao Xue suggested Western food. Chen Guiliang found a moderately priced restaurant.

Chen Guiliang also had some things to do in the afternoon. After lunch, he sat with them for a while. He planned to let the two girls go shopping by themselves, and he would take them back to school after he was done with his errands.

Tao Xue was very considerate. "No need, it's not far anyway. We'll just take a stroll and walk back. Senior, if you have things to do, go ahead. We can't hold up your work."

"How about I take you back to Renmin University now?" Chen Guiliang said.

Li Qian said, "We still want to walk around here."

Chen Guiliang drove back to the company. Instead of going upstairs immediately, he called Li Jian.

The two had only met once. After exchanging phone numbers, Chen Guiliang's only contact with him had been inviting Li Jian to join Xiaonei.

Upon receiving the call, Li Jian was a bit puzzled. "Mr. Chen, hello. Have you written another song?"

"No," Chen Guiliang said. "Do you still remember the original singer of 'The Wind Rises'?"

Li Jian said, "I remember. She's very pretty."

Li Jian thought for a moment and said, "The commemorative edition CD transcription of Abing's original wire recording. It was recorded last year, and there are only a few dozen copies in the whole country."

"How do I get my hands on it? How much does it cost?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Jian said, "It's not that expensive. The regular version is two or three hundred RMB, you can buy it in many places. There are only a few dozen copies of the commemorative edition. The price is probably around twenty or thirty thousand, but for now, no one is willing to sell."

"Bro, don't mess with me. Tell me something I can actually buy," Chen Guiliang said, not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

Li Jian asked, "Then you should stop mentioning traditional music. Name a modern singer she likes."

Chen Guiliang said, "Lo Ta-yu and Stefanie Sun."

"Then get her a signed first edition vinyl of Lo Ta-yu's 'Zhihuzheye'," Li Jian suggested.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Is that thing easy to get?"

Li Jian said, "It's definitely easier to get than Abing's commemorative edition. A signed copy is around 10,000, give or take two or three thousand depending on the situation. At most, it could sell for 15,000. If you can offer 25,000, I can help you contact a music store over in Taiwan. Also, you'll have to cover the airfare and accommodation. They'll definitely deliver it in person; you can't mail something like this."

"Then I'll have to trouble you. If you need anything in the future, give me a call," Chen Guiliang promised.

Li Jian chuckled, "Alright then. I'll start contacting people for you, but I can't guarantee a timeline. If the music store doesn't have it themselves, they'll have to help find another seller."

Chen Guiliang said, "Since I'm already troubling you with one thing, could you help me get a record player that can play vinyls?"

"That's easy. Just wait for my call," Li Jian readily agreed.

Girls needed to be coaxed, their emotional needs had to be met. Chen Guiliang felt he had been negligent in this aspect.

After finishing his work in the afternoon, Chen Guiliang drove over to pick up Bian Guanyue.

Bian Guanyue seemed to have forgotten everything. She was as talkative and cheerful as ever, but she didn't mention Tao Xue at all.

When they arrived at the house jointly registered under both their names, Bian Guanyue happily went to buy groceries and cook, as if she were already living the married life in advance.

Chen Guiliang didn't mention the vinyl record either, planning to give her a surprise later.

In the blink of an eye, it was the end of November.

Panda Burning Incense began to spread on a small scale, and antivirus software like Rising also developed specific countermeasures. The impact wasn't significant for now, but the virus had already entered a period of rapid mutation.

It was getting more and more powerful!

Chen Guiliang called Dong Qianqiu and Guo Feng over, telling them to assign dedicated personnel to monitor Panda Burning Incense and its variants at all times. He even notified Tao Chenggang.

Li Jian hadn't gotten the vinyl record yet, and Chen Guiliang already had to go receive the "Ten Outstanding Young Persons of Beijing" award, as well as take this year's CET-4 English exam.

He had been cramming for a month, and now he felt that CET-4 would be a breeze.
